addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Higgsfield
Use generate_image, generate_video, and generate_audio as the core tools for image, video, and audio creation. Use generate_3d to turn an image into a 3D GLB mesh. When unsure which generation model fits, call models_explore(action:'recommend') with the user's goal and input context before calling a generate_* tool. For edits to an existing asset, prefer the dedicated tool over re-generating with a model: upscale_image / upscale_video (enhance or increase resolution to 2K/4K), outpaint_image (expand or uncrop an image), reframe (change a video's aspect ratio), remove_background (cutout / transparent background), motion_control (recast / puppeteer / motion transfer). Use virality_predictor when the user asks to predict video virality or analyze engagement, attention, audience response, retention risk, hook strength, or creative performance. Before creating or editing any browser game, call get_game_creation_instructions. When those game instructions require a bundled reference, script, or scaffold file, call get_game_creation_bundle_file. Before building any multi-step, made-to-brief video from a user request — a narrated explainer or story video, an ad / commercial, a UGC / talking-head video, a podcast, and similar templated video workflows — call get_workflow_instructions first (with no argument) to see the catalog of available workflows and their triggers, then call it again with the matching workflow name to load its instructions. New workflows are discovered from the catalog, so always check it rather than assuming which exist. When a loaded workflow requires a bundled template, reference, or script file, call get_workflow_bundle_file. When an Apps UI-capable client user has a local photo/image/video/audio for Higgsfield generation input, immediately call media_upload_widget; do not ask them to attach local media in Claude chat because remote MCP tools cannot read those attachments. For voice creation, use create_voice instead. For voice creation in Apps UI-capable clients, call create_voice immediately when… [truncated]

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

#59 - Report Generation Across All Industry Verticals
What & Why
Merchants need to get their data out — for accountants, landlords needing end-of-month statements, tradespeople chasing overdue clients, and retailers reconciling with their bank. Each vertical has different reporting needs driven by real NZ business workflows (GST returns, property managers' rent rolls, trades aged receivables). This adds a "Generate Report" entry point to every analytics/dashboard page across all three verticals, producing downloadable PDFs and CSVs with zero new backend dependencies (all data is already fetched client-side).

Reports per Vertical
Retail / Payments (3 reports)
1. Sales Summary Report Period-level overview: gross revenue, transaction count, average transaction value, breakdown of completed / failed / refunded transactions, net revenue after refunds, GST component (NZ 15%: amount ÷ 1.15 × 0.15), and a split-payment sub-total. One page. PDF output.

2. Transaction Ledger Full line-by-line export: date/time, item name, amount, status (Completed / Refunded / Failed), split indicator. Running subtotals at the bottom. This is the document a merchant emails to their accountant. PDF + CSV.

3. Refunds Report All refunded transactions in the selected period: original date, item, original amount, refund amount, net received. Only offered when at least one refund exists. PDF.

Property Management (4 reports)
1. Rent Roll (industry-standard document) A snapshot (not period-filtered) of every active tenant: property address, tenant name, weekly/fortnightly/monthly rent, last payment received, current status (Paid / Overdue / Sent), outstanding balance. Sorted by property address. This is what every property manager hands to an owner. PDF only (formal document).

2. Collection Statement Period-filtered: every invoice sent, one row each — date, tenant, property, amount, status, paid date. Footer totals: total invoiced, total collected, collection rate %, count of overdue invoices. PDF + CSV.

3. Aged Arrears Report All currently overdue invoices grouped into age buckets: 1–7 days, 8–30 days, 31–60 days, 60+ days. Each row: tenant name, email, property address, invoice amount, days overdue. Bucket subtotals + grand total at risk. Used to escalate collections. PDF only.

4. Annual Income Statement Full year view (hardcoded to calendar year or financial year): rent collected per property, broken out month by month in columns, annual total per property, grand total. GST breakdown if merchant is GST-registered. Suitable for handing to an NZ accountant or including with an IR3R property income return. PDF only.

Trades (4 reports)
1. Invoice Summary Report Period-filtered: all trade invoices, grouped by job type. Each group shows: invoice count, total invoiced, total collected, collection rate %. A GST summary block (using the gstAmount column already stored per invoice): total excl-GST, total GST, total incl-GST. PDF + CSV.

2. Quote Conversion Report All quotes in the selected period: status breakdown (Draft / Sent / Accepted / Rejected / Expired) with count and total value per status. Conversion rate = Accepted ÷ Sent. Average quote value. Average time from sent to accepted (where available). Helps a tradesperson understand their sales pipeline. PDF.

3. Aged Receivables Report All outstanding trade invoices, bucketed identically to Property Aged Arrears (1–7, 8–30, 31–60, 60+). Each row: client name, email, site address, job type, invoice amount, days overdue. Bucket and grand totals. This is used to chase payment. PDF only.

4. Client Statement Either a single client (user selects from a dropdown in the modal) or all clients. For each client: every invoice in the period with status and paid date, balance outstanding. Professional letter format — looks like a statement a firm would post to a debtor. PDF only (the PDF itself gets emailed or printed).

Shared Infrastructure to Build
client/src/lib/report-utils.ts
Utility functions used by all report files:

fmtNZD(cents) — formats cents to "$1,234.56 NZD"
fmtDate(date) — NZ date format (dd/mm/yyyy)
calcGST(centsInclGST) — returns { excl, gst, incl } at NZ 15% rate
buildCSV(headers, rows) — builds a CSV string and triggers a browser download
printReport(htmlString, title) — opens a new browser window, injects the HTML (which includes @page { size: A4; margin: 18mm; } and the brand header CSS), then calls window.print(). The user saves as PDF from the browser's native print dialog. Zero npm dependencies.
dateRangeLabel(start, end) — human-readable period label for report headers
client/src/components/reports/ReportModal.tsx
A shared bottom-sheet style modal (matching the app's existing mobile-first design) that:

Lists available report types for the current vertical as selectable cards
Offers a date range picker: presets matching existing timeframe pills (day / week / month / year) plus a "Custom" option with two date inputs
For Client Statement: adds a client selector dropdown (populated from already-fetched client data)
Has two action buttons: "Download CSV" (where applicable) and "Generate PDF"
Uses the existing app colour scheme (no new design tokens)
Report template files (one per vertical)
Each file exports functions that accept the already-fetched invoice/transaction arrays and a date range, compute the report data, and return an HTML string ready for printReport() and a data array ready for buildCSV().

client/src/components/reports/retailReports.ts — 3 retail reports
client/src/components/reports/propertyReports.ts — 4 property reports
client/src/components/reports/tradesReports.ts — 4 trades reports
PDF brand header (included in every report HTML string)
Merchant business name (from the merchant profile already in app state)
GST number and NZBN (already stored in the merchant record)
Report title + period
"Generated by TaptPay · {date}" footer with page numbers via CSS counter
Entry Points (where the Generate button lives)
Vertical    File    Placement
Retail    client/src/pages/dashboard.tsx    Icon button in the top-right of the header, alongside existing nav icons
Property    client/src/pages/property/property-analytics.tsx    Right side of the "Payment History" h2 row in the swipeable sheet
Property (dashboard)    client/src/pages/property/property-dashboard.tsx    Same position in dashboard header
Trades    client/src/pages/trades/trades-analytics.tsx    Right side of the "Payment History" h2 row
Trades (dashboard)    client/src/pages/trades/trades-dashboard.tsx    Same position in dashboard header
The button is a small icon button (document/download icon from lucide-react) labelled "Export" — compact enough not to crowd the existing UI.

Done Looks Like
A small "Export" button appears on every analytics and dashboard page across all three verticals.
Tapping it opens a bottom-sheet modal listing the available reports for that vertical.
Choosing a report type, selecting a date range, and tapping "Generate PDF" opens a new browser tab with a print dialog — the user saves as PDF.
Where CSV is available, "Download CSV" saves the file directly.
Every PDF includes the merchant's business name, GST number, NZBN, the report period, and a TaptPay footer.
All amounts are NZD. GST calculations use 15%.
Reports only use data already in the TanStack Query cache — no new API endpoints are needed.
No new npm packages are added.
Out of Scope
Server-side PDF rendering (not needed; browser print-to-PDF is sufficient for NZ SMB use)
Scheduled / emailed reports (future feature)
Admin-level cross-merchant reporting
The retail merchant-terminal.tsx page (that is the payment entry screen, not an analytics view)
Steps
Build report-utils.ts — shared utilities: NZD formatter, NZ date formatter, GST calculator, CSV download helper, printReport() (new-window + print), date range label.
Build ReportModal.tsx — mobile-first modal component: report type card list, timeframe/custom date picker, optional client selector for Client Statement, CSV and PDF action buttons. Accept vertical, reportTypes, and data props.
Build retailReports.ts — implement Sales Summary, Transaction Ledger, and Refunds Report HTML/CSV generators. Use merchant profile for brand header.
Build propertyReports.ts — implement Rent Roll, Collection Statement, Aged Arrears, Annual Income Statement generators. Rent Roll uses all active tenants regardless of date filter.
Build tradesReports.ts — implement Invoice Summary, Quote Conversion, Aged Receivables, Client Statement generators. Quote Conversion fetches from /api/trades/quotes (already available).
Wire up Retail — add Export button to dashboard.tsx, connect ReportModal with retail report types and currently fetched transaction data.
Wire up Property — add Export button to property-analytics.tsx and property-dashboard.tsx, pass tenant + invoice data to the modal.
Wire up Trades — add Export button to trades-analytics.tsx and trades-dashboard.tsx, pass client + invoice data (and quotes, fetched on demand) to the modal.

client/src/lib/trades-api.ts

content.text:
I now have enough to give you a grounded review. I verified the plan's key claims against the actual schema and app setup rather than taking them at face value — and the most important claim doesn't hold.

## The one that blocks the whole approach

**`printReport()` (new window + `window.print()`) will not work in your iOS app.** This is a Capacitor app (`@capacitor/ios` in `package.json`, `ios/App` present). In a WKWebView:
- `window.open('', …)` to get a writable document handle returns `null` — there are no real popup windows.
- `window.print()` is a no-op on iOS WKWebView.

So on the primary (mobile) target, "Generate PDF" would silently do nothing. Note your existing `window.open` calls (`SmartTransitions.jsx`, `merchant-url-display.tsx`) are all `mailto:`/`sms:`/external-URL — there's **no precedent that print works here**, because it doesn't. This is a "mobile-first app" whose PDF strategy only works in a desktop browser tab.

What I'd do instead: either (a) render the report HTML into an in-app route/component and use the Capacitor print/share plugin or `@capacitor/share` + a generated file, or (b) if you truly want print-to-PDF, accept it's a **desktop-web-only** feature and gate the Export button off in the native shell. Decide this before writing any of the three report files, because it changes what `printReport` even is. Worth a quick spike on one report end-to-end in the actual iOS build before committing to the pattern.

## Factual errors in the plan

1. **"GST summary block (using the `gstAmount` column already stored per invoice)" — that column does not exist.** `jobInvoices` (schema.ts:1042) has only `amountCents`; no GST split. GST lives on `quotes` (`gstCents`, `gstMode`, schema.ts:998–999) — but a job invoice can be a *quick invoice* with `quoteId = null`, so it has **no** GST data at all. For those you'd have to derive GST from `merchant.tradeGstMode` (`inclusive` → `amount/1.15*0.15`) — the same formula the plan uses for retail. So the plan is internally inconsistent (retail derives, trades "reads a column") and the trades path is underspecified. Pick one derivation and apply it everywhere.

2. **Quote statuses are wrong.** Plan lists Draft / Sent / Accepted / **Rejected** / Expired. Actual (schema.ts:995): `draft · sent · viewed · accepted · declined · expired`. "Rejected" is `declined`, and there's a `viewed` state the plan ignores. This breaks **Quote Conversion**: "Conversion rate = Accepted ÷ Sent" divides by only quotes *currently* in `sent` — but an accepted quote is no longer in `sent`. You need `accepted ÷ (every quote that was ever sent)`, i.e. count anything not still in draft. Define this precisely or the headline number is nonsense.

3. **"Overdue" / "Sent" / "Paid" aren't stored statuses.** Both `invoicesRentRequests` (schema.ts) and `jobInvoices` default to `pending_dispatch`; overdue is *derived* (`dueAt < now && !paidAt`). Rent Roll and Collection Statement need a defined status-derivation helper, not a column read.

## Data-availability — mostly OK for property, flag for the rest

The premise "all data is already in the TanStack cache" **checks out for property**: `usePropertyInvoices()`/`usePropertyTenants()` (property-data.ts:26–31) fetch `/api/property/invoices` and `/api/property/tenants` with **no window/limit params**, so Rent Roll (all tenants), Aged Arrears (all overdue), and Annual Income Statement (full year) are derivable client-side — *provided the server endpoint isn't itself paginated/capped*. **Verify the server returns full history** before relying on the Annual statement; that's the one report that silently under-reports if there's a default `LIMIT`.

Two caveats the plan glosses:
- **Quotes are not cached on those pages** — the plan admits "fetched on demand," which contradicts "no new API endpoints / only cache data." It's fine (the endpoint exists), just stop claiming zero new fetches.
- **Retail split & refund data live in separate tables** (`splitPayments` schema.ts:185, `refunds` schema.ts:208). The Sales Summary "split-payment sub-total" and Refunds Report need those to actually be in cache on `dashboard.tsx`. Confirm they are, or the numbers come out zero.

## Things I'd add

- **A test step.** These are accountant- and IRD-facing financial documents and the plan has zero tests. At minimum unit-test the pure compute functions (GST, aged buckets, collection/conversion rates, per-property annual totals) with fixtures. Given your recent jest work, this is cheap insurance against a wrong GST figure going to a real accountant.
- **CSV hardening in `buildCSV`.** (a) Escape commas/quotes/newlines — tenant names, `jobDetails`, addresses will contain them. (b) **Formula-injection guard**: prefix cells starting with `= + - @` with `'`. User-controlled names in a CSV opened in Excel are an injection vector — relevant given your recent security audit.
- **GST gating.** Only the property Annual statement gates on `merchant.gstRegistered`. A non-GST-registered merchant seeing a "GST component" on the retail Sales Summary or trades Invoice Summary is wrong. Gate *all* GST display on `gstRegistered`.
- **Integer/rounding discipline.** `amount ÷ 1.15 × 0.15` in float, summed per-line, drifts cents vs. computing on the total. Do integer-cent math and decide line-level vs. total-level GST once — accountants notice a 1c mismatch.
- **Timezone.** Format and compute period boundaries in `Pacific/Auckland`, not UTC. A payment at 11pm NZ on the last of the month falls into the wrong GST period otherwise. This affects `fmtDate`, `periodWindow`, and every report header.
- **Shared aged-bucket util.** Property Aged Arrears and Trades Aged Receivables are "bucketed identically" — put the bucketer in `report-utils.ts`, don't duplicate across `propertyReports.ts`/`tradesReports.ts`.
- **Empty/zero states.** Divide-by-zero on collection rate, conversion rate, avg quote value when the period is empty. And "Refunds Report only when a refund exists" needs a defined empty-state everywhere else too.

## Smaller notes

- **Financial year is undecided** ("calendar year or financial year"). NZ tax year is 1 Apr–31 Mar and IR3R is annual — pick NZ tax year as default, and consider letting the merchant choose the year rather than hardcoding "this year."
- **Merchant profile availability**: confirm business name / `gstNumber` / `nzbn` are in a cached query on *all five* entry-point pages (retail vs. property vs. trades may load the merchant differently). The brand header breaks silently if not.
- **Large ledgers**: a full-year Transaction Ledger could be thousands of `<tr>` in one print window — fine, but worth a mental note for perf.

---

**Bottom line:** the vertical-by-vertical report catalogue is well-scoped and the property data model genuinely supports it. But before building anything I'd (1) resolve the **Capacitor print viability** question — it may invalidate `printReport` entirely, (2) fix the **`gstAmount`/quote-status** factual errors, and (3) add **tests + CSV hardening**. Steps 1–2 of the plan (`report-utils.ts`, `ReportModal.tsx`) are safe to start, but I'd spike one full report through to a real iOS build first.

Want me to prototype the print path in the iOS shell to settle #1, or draft the corrected `report-utils.ts` (with the timezone/GST/CSV fixes) so the foundation is right?

Everything I need is confirmed. Here's the key discovery that reshapes the plan: **`jspdf`, `html2canvas`, and `recharts` are already dependencies** (`package.json`), and there's **no `@capacitor/share`** yet. So the right answer isn't browser print-to-PDF (which is dead in your WKWebView) — it's **client-side vector PDF generation that outputs a real file, shared through the native share sheet.**

Here's the plan.

---

## Plan #59b — Branded, shareable PDF reports (+ CSV) across all verticals

### The approach, and why

The original plan's `printReport()` (new window + `window.print()`) is a non-starter in the Capacitor iOS shell. Instead, **generate the PDF entirely in JS with jsPDF**, then hand the file to the OS share sheet. This:

- **Works in the WKWebView** — pure JS, no popup, no print dialog.
- Produces a **real vector PDF** — crisp selectable text, small files, the kind of thing an accountant or landlord actually accepts (not a blurry screenshot, not a spreadsheet).
- Is **shareable natively** — Files, Mail, AirDrop, WhatsApp — via `@capacitor/share`, and downloads as a Blob on web.
- **Reuses installed deps** (`jspdf`), keeping with the low-dependency ethos. The only adds are tiny companions.

CSV stays exactly as before — it's the "give me the raw rows" export. The PDF is the new polished, brand-forward artefact.

### Engine decision (recommended: jsPDF + jspdf-autotable)

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **jsPDF + `jspdf-autotable`** ✅ | Already have jsPDF. autotable gives auto multi-page tables, repeating headers, and page-number footers for free — exactly what ledgers/rent-rolls/statements need. Vector text. Full control over a branded header band + KPI cards. **Recommended.** |
| `@react-pdf/renderer` | Nicer for magazine-style layout, but heavier and table pagination is manual. Overkill for table-driven financial docs. |
| Server-side (Puppeteer) | Best fidelity, but new backend + headless-Chrome infra on Replit. You explicitly wanted zero backend; save for later if these prove insufficient. |

New deps: `jspdf-autotable` (~one small, ubiquitous companion), `@capacitor/share`, `@capacitor/filesystem`. If you'd rather I go the `@react-pdf` route for a more designed look at the cost of trickier tables, say so and I'll re-cut the plan.

### The PDF design system (`report-pdf-theme.ts`)

One shared theme so all 11 reports look like one product, matching the app:

- **Brand green** `hsl(155 40% 25%)` (your `--primary`) as the header band + accent; white on green.
- **Cover/summary block**: report title, period, and a row of **KPI cards** (big number + label in rounded rects) — e.g. Gross Revenue / Txns / Avg Value / GST. This is the "beautiful, not-a-spreadsheet" first impression.
- **One chart per summary** where it earns its place (revenue-by-bucket bar, quote-conversion donut, aged-arrears stacked bar). Rendered off-screen via **recharts → high-res PNG (`html2canvas`) embedded as an image**; all surrounding text stays vector. Text stays sharp, only the chart is raster.
- **Tables** via autotable: zebra striping, right-aligned money, brand-green header row, automatic page breaks with repeating column headers.
- **Header on every page**: merchant business name, `gstNumber`, `nzbn` (from the cached merchant profile). **Footer**: "Generated by TaptPay · {NZ date} · Page X of Y".
- Embed one brand font via `jsPDF.addFont` (there's no font asset in the repo yet — I'll add a woff/ttf, or fall back to Helvetica if you'd rather not ship a font binary).

### Files (revised from the original)

```
client/src/lib/report-utils.ts        fmtNZD, fmtDate (NZ tz), calcGST, buildCSV(+injection guard), agedBuckets, dateRangeLabel
client/src/lib/report-pdf.ts          jsPDF engine: brandHeader, kpiRow, chartImage, table, footer, savePdf(share/download)
client/src/lib/report-pdf-theme.ts    colors, fonts, spacing, KPI-card + table styles
client/src/components/reports/ReportModal.tsx     shared bottom-sheet: report cards, date presets+custom, client selector, [Download CSV] [Generate PDF]
client/src/components/reports/retailReports.ts    3 reports → {pdf(doc), csv()}
client/src/components/reports/propertyReports.ts  4 reports
client/src/components/reports/tradesReports.ts     4 reports
client/src/lib/__tests__/report-utils.test.ts     GST, buckets, rates, CSV escaping
```

Each report exports a `pdf(doc, data, period, merchant)` that draws into the shared jsPDF doc, plus a `csv(data, period)`. The engine and theme are the only things that touch jsPDF — report files just call `kpiRow(...)`, `table(...)`, etc.

### The share pipeline (`savePdf`)

```
const blob = doc.output('blob')
if (Capacitor.isNativePlatform()) {
   write blob → Filesystem (Cache dir) → Share.share({ url: fileUri })   // native share sheet
} else if (navigator.canShare?.({ files })) {
   navigator.share({ files: [file] })                                     // web share where supported
} else {
   trigger <a download> on an object URL                                  // desktop fallback
}
```

### Baked-in fixes from my earlier review

- **GST is derived, uniformly**, from `merchant.tradeGstMode`/15% — there is no `gstAmount` column; quotes have `gstCents`, quick invoices have none. Integer-cent math, GST computed on totals. **All GST display gated on `merchant.gstRegistered`.**
- **Quote Conversion uses real statuses** (`draft·sent·viewed·accepted·declined·expired`); conversion = accepted ÷ (everything ever sent), not ÷ current-`sent`.
- **"Overdue"/"Sent"/"Paid" derived** from `dueAt`/`paidAt`, not read as a status column.
- **Shared `agedBuckets()` util** for Property Aged Arrears + Trades Aged Receivables.
- **NZ timezone** (`Pacific/Auckland`) for all dates and period boundaries.
- **CSV injection guard** + proper escaping.
- **Empty/zero-division states** for every rate and every empty period.
- **Verify `/api/property/invoices` returns full history** (not server-capped) before trusting the Annual Income Statement.

### Steps

1. **Spike first (de-risk):** wire jsPDF → Filesystem → `@capacitor/share` for one trivial report on the **real iOS build**, confirm the share sheet and a valid PDF. *Nothing else proceeds until this works.*
2. Build `report-utils.ts` + tests (pure functions, no PDF).
3. Build `report-pdf-theme.ts` + `report-pdf.ts` engine (header/KPI/chart/table/footer/savePdf).
4. Build `ReportModal.tsx`.
5. `retailReports.ts` (Sales Summary, Ledger, Refunds) — validate against a real merchant's data.
6. `propertyReports.ts` (Rent Roll, Collection Statement, Aged Arrears, Annual Income).
7. `tradesReports.ts` (Invoice Summary, Quote Conversion, Aged Receivables, Client Statement); fetch quotes on demand.
8. Wire the Export button into all five pages (`dashboard.tsx`, `property-analytics/-dashboard.tsx`, `trades-analytics/-dashboard.tsx`).
9. `/verify` one report per vertical end-to-end in the iOS build.

### Decisions I need from you

1. **Ship a brand font binary** in the PDF, or use built-in Helvetica? (Font makes it noticeably more "designed.")
2. **Charts on the summary pages** — yes (recommended, it's the main "beautiful" lever) or keep it clean type-only?
3. Confirm **jsPDF + autotable** over `@react-pdf`.

I can **re-draw those exact charts as vector in the PDF** — no blurry screenshots, pixel-faithful to the app, and it reuses your existing `buildBuckets`/`buildBilledBuckets` helpers.

Here's the finalized plan.

---

## Plan #59 (final) — Designed, on-brand, shareable PDF reports (+ CSV)

### Engine & why
**`@react-pdf/renderer`** — the more-designed route you asked for. Component-based layout (cover pages, KPI cards, real typographic tables), runs entirely in the WKWebView (outputs a Blob, no print dialog — which is dead in your Capacitor shell), and its `<Svg>` primitives let me port your charts as **vector**. CSV stays as the raw-data export alongside it.

New deps: `@react-pdf/renderer`, `@capacitor/share`, `@capacitor/filesystem`. (jsPDF/html2canvas stay unused for this — we don't need rasterization.)

### Brand system (pulled from your code, not invented)
- **Navy `#040D6D`** — cover band, headers, table header rows, chart bars, primary text.
- **Sky `#58ABFF`** — accents, KPI highlights, value labels, chart selection/secondary series.
- **Off-white `#F6F8FC`** — page and card backgrounds.
- **Typeface: Outfit** (the app's font) registered via `Font.register` — I'll bundle the TTF so it renders in the native shell. This is what makes it read as "designed" and matches the app 1:1.

### Charts — "like the app, digestible to all"
Port the bespoke dashboard chart into a reusable `<ReportBarChart>` built from `@react-pdf` Svg primitives:
- Solid **navy** bars (collected), dashed **sky** wireframe "ghost" bars (billed/outstanding) — the exact visual language of `RentBarChart`.
- Sky value labels, tabular-nums, rounded bar tops.
- Fed by the **existing** `buildBuckets()` / `buildBilledBuckets()` (property-dashboard-data.ts) so the PDF chart and the on-screen chart can never disagree.
- Kept deliberately simple: one clear bar chart per summary (revenue/rent by period; aged-arrears as a stacked bar; quote-conversion as a compact donut). No dense multi-axis charts — legible to a landlord or accountant at a glance.

### Files
```
client/src/lib/report-utils.ts          fmtNZD, fmtDate (NZ tz), calcGST, buildCSV(+injection guard), agedBuckets, dateRangeLabel
client/src/lib/report-pdf/theme.ts       navy/sky/off-white tokens, Outfit registration, spacing, table & KPI styles
client/src/lib/report-pdf/components.tsx  <CoverBand> <KpiRow> <ReportBarChart> <DonutStat> <DataTable> <BrandHeader> <PageFooter>

client/src/components/reports/ReportModal.tsx     bottom-sheet: report cards, date presets+custom, client selector, [Download CSV] [Generate PDF]
client/src/components/reports/retailReports.tsx    3 reports → { Doc, csv }

client/src/components/reports/tradesReports.tsx     4 reports
client/src/lib/__tests__/report-utils.test.ts      GST, buckets, rates, CSV escaping

Each report exports a `<Document>` (built from the shared components) + a `csv()`. Only `report-pdf/*` touches `@react-pdf`; report files just compose `<KpiRow>`, `<ReportBarChart>`, `<DataTable>`.

```
const blob = await pdf(<ReportDoc/>).toBlob()
native → Filesystem.write(Cache) → Share.share({ url })      // iOS share sheet: Files, Mail, WhatsApp…
web   → navigator.share({files}) ?? <a download>            // fallback
